records.record_key: title:war by algorithm giambattista vico and ethics of war in the techno logical era|year:2019
records.title: War by Algorithm: Giambattista Vico and Ethics of War in the Techno-Logical Era
source_evidence: The institutional record identifies John Robert Emery, a 2019 UC Irvine political-science dissertation, and a 220-page PDF.
The abstract and pages 13, 179, and 200-201 discuss meaningful human control, algorithmic targeting, removal from lethal action, and the limits of technical control claims.
Full-text searches found no audit or protocol procedure equivalent to the repository method.
records.screening_rationale: The dissertation supplies a material construct and historical mechanism for loss of practical control. It does not disclose the tested integration.
records.limits: The record is a dissertation and does not estimate whether a documentary practical-control procedure is reliable or institutionally effective.
records.ai_assistance: AI located and inspected the institutional full text, proposed the bounded screening decision, and recorded page-level support.

records.title: Ensuring Lethal Autonomous Weapon Systems Comply with International Humanitarian Law
source_evidence: The SSRN record identifies Maziar Homayounnejad, TLI Think! Paper 85/2017, 69 pages, posted 10 December 2017 and revised 23 January 2018.
The abstract states that the paper applies distinction, proportionality, precautions, and meaningful human control to lawful LAWS development and use.
The retrieval surface exposed the abstract and PDF locator, while direct text inspection of the PDF was blocked by the publisher delivery surface.
records.screening_rationale: The source supplies legal and operational background for meaningful human control. The recovered abstract does not disclose the repository's integrated reconstruction procedure.
records.limits: Only the declared purpose and scope may be used until full text is inspected.
records.ai_assistance: AI located the publisher abstract, proposed the bounded screening decision, and recorded the abstract-only limit.

records.record_key: title:disentangled concept residual models bridging the interpretability performance gap for incomplete concept sets|year:2026
records.title: Disentangled Concept-Residual Models: Bridging the Interpretability-Performance Gap for Incomplete Concept Sets
source_evidence: The official record identifies a January 2026 Transactions on Machine Learning Research publication and an 18-page paper.
The paper defines concept-residual overlap and reports that a corrected human-readable concept can fail to change the output when the residual path retains conflicting information.
The paper reports intervention and overlap results across five datasets, while its unit of analysis is model architecture rather than a public incident record.
records.screening_rationale: The source supplies a material causal mechanism: nominal intervenability can fail when a parallel information path defeats the correction. It does not disclose historical case reconstruction, evidence fitness, or conclusion closure.
records.limits: Its model tests do not establish human performance, institutional control, or field effects.
records.ai_assistance: AI located and inspected the official full text, proposed the bounded screening decision, and recorded page-level support.

records.title: Effective Human Oversight of GenAI-Powered Legal Research Tools
routes_checked: American Association of Law Libraries publisher PDF
source_evidence: The frozen Semantic Scholar record preserves the AALL PDF locator even though exact-title search returned no matching record.
The publisher PDF rendered as 20 pages. Its cover identifies Law Library Journal, volume 118, number 3, 2026.
The retrieval channel did not expose a readable text layer. The source record names B. Mills while the filename names Jennings.
records.screening_rationale: OPEN: Source access is established. A substantive decision would exceed the readable evidence available in this run.
records.limits: The author must read the rendered paper and resolve the author-name mismatch before assigning a v0.7 screening decision.
records.ai_assistance: AI recovered and visually verified the publisher PDF, recorded the extraction and metadata limits, and made no substantive screening decision.

records.title: The Loop Is Broken: Why Autonomous-warfare Policy Must Reckon with Human Performance
routes_checked: International Institute for Strategic Studies issue page
source_evidence: The publisher record identifies Anna M. Gielas, Survival 67(4), pages 57-66, published online 25 July 2025.
The abstract argues that human-in-the-loop and meaningful-human-control labels can omit human-performance constraints and proposes a human-in-the-mesh model.
The publisher keywords and notes identify the Patriot missile-defence system, human control, human-machine interaction, workload, and adaptive automation.
records.screening_rationale: The source directly overlaps the paper's practical-control mechanism and one case family. It is a close source even though it does not disclose the full repository procedure in the inspected material.
records.limits: The abstract may support a bounded statement about the source's declared model. Full text is required for proposition-specific use beyond that statement.
records.ai_assistance: AI located the publisher abstract and official issue summary, proposed the close-source decision, and recorded the full-text limit.

claim_boundary: This tranche records retrieval and four bounded screening decisions. It does not estimate residual close-source prevalence, close the 284-record sample, establish exhaustive search coverage, or permit claims beyond an inspected abstract or full text.
